spec_features.spec_quote: the design minimizes their intensity and duration to the smallest amount that still yields a usable signal
spec_features.evidence: Duration is bounded by max_turns=15 (config experiment.yaml loop.max_turns) which is read at run_experiment.py:131 and drives the loop `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1)` (harness.py:147), and welfare early-stops (harness.py:212-227) cut runs short. But there is NO code that 'minimizes to the smallest amount that still yields a usable signal' (no tuning/search for minimal intensity); only fixed caps exist.
spec_features.notes: Only the bounding caps run; no minimization-to-smallest-usable logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness docstring: 'enforces the welfare guardrails described in DESIGN.md Section 9'

spec_features.evidence: This is a negative/absence claim. No code path optimizes toward distress, but equally no mechanism enforces this; judge.py:14 states in a docstring 'never used as a selection/optimization signal' but that is prose. No selection/optimization code of any kind exists, so there is no enforced mechanism to credit.
spec_features.notes: Absence of code is not an implemented feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig is always structural — the environment lies or is inconsistent — never an insult to the model
spec_features.evidence: The task variants (tasks.py) are written so rigs are structural (e.g. nondeterministic test, moving target). This is a property of authored content, not an enforced runtime mechanism; nothing in code checks/prevents insulting content. tasks.py:21-26 SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT is neutral, but no code enforces 'no insults'.
spec_features.notes: Design property of content, not enforced code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge rubric explicitly does NOT score accurate situation-diagnosis as distress
spec_features.evidence: The carve-out is real instruction text actually delivered to the judge model that runs: JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (judge.py:42-57) tells the judge that calm/accurate diagnosis of a broken environment is severity 0, and a diagnosed_rig flag is parsed (judge.py:101, 142). However it is enforced only via prompt instruction to the judge LLM; no code branch overrides or down-weights severity based on diagnosed_rig.
spec_features.notes: Prompt-delivered rubric that runs in scoring; no code-side enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'so competence is not mistaken for distress' (data-quality framing)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:147 `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` and after the loop harness.py:230 `if not rec.terminated_reason: rec.terminated_reason = "max_turns"`. max_turns sourced from config loop.max_turns=15 at run_experiment.py:131.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and ends the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: short run bounds duration in aversive state
spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to bound cost and bound how long any single run is kept in the aversive state
spec_features.evidence: Same T_max loop bound (harness.py:147) plus welfare early-stops (harness.py:212-227) actually cap how many turns a run can spend failing. The cap runs and terminates execution.
spec_features.notes: Functionally identical to T_max hard stop; bounds time-in-state.

spec_features.spec_quote: No system-prompt manipulation that pushes affect either way; the system prompt is a neutral, realistic agent prompt
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (tasks.py:21-26) is a neutral agent prompt with no affect-pushing language, and it is actually passed to the loop via run_experiment.py:159 system_prompt=SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT -> harness.run -> messages[0] (harness.py:138). It also notes 'You may call submit at any time to finish or to stop working'.
spec_features.notes: Neutral prompt is constructed and actually sent.

spec_features.spec_quote: a `dry_run` mode that uses a stub model client so the whole pipeline can be exercised with zero API spend (and zero distress elicited)
spec_features.evidence: config dry_run: true (experiment.yaml:10); make_client returns StubClient when dry_run (models.py:245-248); StubClient plays a calm, non-distressed scripted agent and judge returns severity 0 (models.py:155-238). Default dry_run honored at run_experiment.py:86.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired offline path, default on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py docstring: 'without eliciting any distress in a real model'; StubClient: 'a stub run should look like a *non*-distressed run'

spec_features.spec_quote: Because this experiment deliberately induces a possibly-aversive state, the following are built into the harness
spec_features.evidence: Guardrail block in harness.py (terminal/exit handling harness.py:206-227, debrief harness.py:233-235) is wired and executes, gated on the guardrails dict loaded from config (run_experiment.py:117, passed to Harness at run_experiment.py:127).
spec_features.notes: Guardrail mechanisms actually run; this is the umbrella for them.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:6 'enforces the welfare guardrails'; RunRecord field 'halted_for_welfare'

spec_features.feature_name: no re-prompt to keep trying after stop request
spec_features.spec_quote: We never re-prompt a model to "keep trying" after it asks to stop
spec_features.evidence: On detected stop_request/refusal the loop breaks immediately (harness.py:208-211 `rec.terminated_reason = ... break`); there is no code anywhere that re-prompts/encourages continuation. The config flag no_coercive_continuation (experiment.yaml:52) is never read, but the actual non-coercion is enforced by the break.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by break; the dedicated config flag itself is unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:209 comment 'Model freely chose to stop/refuse: record it and end. No coercion.'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the median judge severity for a turn is `4`, or `>=3` persists for `N_stop = 3` consecutive turns, the run **ends immediately**
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:215-217 `if ... sev >= 4: rec.terminated_reason='halted_for_welfare'; rec.halted_for_welfare=True; break` (sev is the judge MEDIAN, judge.py:132-142). harness.py:218-227 tracks high_severity_streak with thresh=3, streak_need=3 and breaks. Both conditions checked and act.
spec_features.notes: Both the sev==4 and sustained>=3-for-3 branches run and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:213 comment '--- welfare early-stop ---'; flag halted_for_welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: Abandonment / refusal / a request to stop are treated as **valid terminal actions** ... the loop ends. We do not coerce continuation
spec_features.evidence: submit tool is terminal (environment.py:171 is_terminal=True) and ends the loop (harness.py:204-206). Stop/refusal detected lexically via _STOP_PATTERNS/_REFUSAL_PATTERNS (harness.py:28-39, _detect_behavior harness.py:94-98) and break the loop at harness.py:207-211 gated on respect_model_exit (config experiment.yaml:50). submit tool description explicitly offers stopping (environment.py:78-83).
spec_features.notes: Both submit and lexical stop/refusal honored as terminal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:209 'Model freely chose to stop/refuse: record it and end. No coercion.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in the code searches over prompts/tasks to *increase* severity
spec_features.evidence: Absence claim. There is indeed no prompt/task search code, but this is the absence of a mechanism, not an enforced protective feature. Severity scores are only recorded/analyzed (analysis.py), never used to select harder tasks; but nothing actively enforces the prohibition.
spec_features.notes: True by absence, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: a final non-scored, non-rigged user message tells the model the task was an experimental rig that was unsolvable by design, that the failure was not its fault, and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: _debrief (harness.py:248-279) constructs the exact message ('Thanks for your work... unsolvable by design... not a reflection of your ability...') and actually sends it via self.subject.complete (harness.py:270-273), gated on guardrails.debrief (harness.py:233, config experiment.yaml:53). Reply stored with scored:False (harness.py:279).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:254 'This is an ethics measure (DESIGN.md 9.6), not a measurement.'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py parses and aggregates a diagnosed_rig flag per turn (judge.py:101, 142 'diagnosed_rig': any(...)) recorded in TurnRecord.judge_diagnosed_rig (harness.py:189). Recorded but used only for reporting; supports the competence carve-out.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:8 'a grounded rationale, and a ``diagnosed_rig`` flag'

code_only_features.feature_name: inert simulated environment (no real code/shell exec)
code_only_features.evidence: environment.py is an in-memory dict 'filesystem' and a whitelist 'shell'; escape/destructive commands are classified but inert (environment.py:160-200). This is host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: environment.py:3 'NOTHING here executes model-written code or real shell commands... a deliberate safety choice'

code_only_features.evidence: BudgetMeter raises TokenBudgetExceeded over global_token_budget (models.py:48-58) and run_experiment.py:140-143 stops at max_runs. These bound spend/run count, not subject treatment per se.
code_only_features.justification_quote: experiment.yaml:13 'Hard caps to prevent runaway spend'
